sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The genius cucullatus was a Celtic god of the Continent and Britain. The name comes from the Latin cucullus, the hood attached to a cloak. These hooded spirits appear across Celtic lands. On the Continent they appear alone. In Britain the cucullati always come as triplets. Their phallus-shaped form marks them as fertility spirits. A group of them looks like small phalluses. Some sculptures reveal a phallus where a man's head should be. British carvings show the hooded dwarfs holding eggs. Their distribution matches the mother goddesses called the Deae Matres. They often appear with these goddesses. One goddess who accompanies them is named Cuda. Their altars bore the cornucopia, the turret crown, and the patera, an offering plate.
